title: Come and see (John 1:35–42)
hookLine: two disciples follow; he asks, what are you looking for?

cards: The next day, John the Baptist is standing with two of his own disciples when Jesus walks past. John says it again: behold the Lamb of God. And the two start walking after Jesus.
Think about what that cost John: his students, leaving. And think what it's like for the two of them, following a stranger at a distance, not sure what they'll say if he notices. Then he does.
He turns around and sees them following. And the first words Jesus speaks in John's whole Gospel are a question.

teach.b: The question, in the King James words: "What seek ye?" What are you looking for? Not who are you, not what do you want from me.
It's a question for anyone, any day.

They answer with a question of their own: "Rabbi, (which is to say, being interpreted, Master,) where dwellest thou?" Where are you staying? They don't want a quick answer in the road; they want to be where he is.
And he says: "Come and see." No speech. No test.

Then John adds a detail only an eyewitness would bother with, many readers think: "for it was about the tenth hour." Around four in the afternoon. Someone remembered the time of day for the rest of their life.
One of the two is named: Andrew. The other is never named, and many Christians through the centuries have thought it was the beloved disciple, though the text doesn't say.
The first thing Andrew does is find his own brother, Simon, and tell him: "We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ."
He brings him to Jesus, and Jesus gives Simon a new name: Cephas, Aramaic for rock. In Greek, Petros. Peter.
Look at the chain: John points, two follow, a question, an invitation, an afternoon, and one of them goes to get his brother.
That's how this Gospel says it began: not with a crowd, but with someone saying, come and see.

how: Many churches celebrate Andrew, the first called, on November 30, and Christians often describe sharing their faith the way he did, by bringing a friend or family member to come and see.

games.q: what's inside John 1:35–42 — tap the pairs.

s: Peter is the first disciple to follow Jesus in John's Gospel
Andrew and another disciple follow first; then Andrew brings his brother Simon.
Jesus's first words in John are a question
John's Gospel names both of the first two disciples
it names Andrew. the other is never named.

games.q: you're one of two people following Jesus down a path. he turns and asks what you're looking for. what do you say?
o: we want you to teach us.
games.why: "Rabbi, where dwellest thou?" they want to be where he is. he says, "come and see."

practice: Let Jesus's first question in John sit in front of you: what are you looking for?

Not what you should want, but what you actually want underneath, peace, to be known, a second chance, rest, and let one honest answer come without fixing or judging it. If you pray, you can tell God your answer.

wordCard.voice: Cephas. The Aramaic name, meaning rock, that Jesus gives Simon when Andrew brings his brother to him, Peter in Greek.

orig.note: Greek: come, and you will see. the invitation in John 1:39.

carryVoice: Your line: what seek ye? A week from Emmaus to the end of Luke, then into John: the Word, the Lamb, and this first invitation. Day five hundred ninety-five, and another week on the path.
